title: Biomechanical Coach Assessment (Deterministic Rules)
disclaimer: Notice: This assessment is generated by an algorithmic sports ergonomic rule set for comfort and performance optimization. It does not constitute a medical or physiotherapeutic diagnosis and does not replace a qualified in-person bike fit evaluation.
insufficient_data_summary: A conclusive postural assessment could not be generated because key joint angles were not recorded or exhibited low detection confidence. Please perform a capture with the athlete clearly framed in the sagittal plane pedaling at a steady cadence.
knee_low: Posture analysis observed marked knee flexion ({measured:.1f}° at BDC compared to the {ideal_min:.0f}°–{ideal_max:.0f}° reference range). This suggests the saddle may be positioned lower than recommended, which tends to increase compressive forces on the anterior knee structures and limits optimal leg extension.
knee_high: Posture analysis observed pronounced knee extension ({measured:.1f}° at BDC compared to the {ideal_min:.0f}°–{ideal_max:.0f}° reference range). This suggests the saddle may be set excessively high, potentially causing pelvic rocking and strain on the hamstrings.
knee_ok: Leg extension at bottom dead center ({measured:.1f}°) lies within the ergonomic reference range ({ideal_min:.0f}°–{ideal_max:.0f}°), suggesting a harmonious relationship between inseam length and saddle height.
knee_missing: Knee angle at BDC was not measured.
torso_low_low_flex: The observed torso inclination ({measured:.1f}°) is pronounced relative to the reported flexibility (low). This more aggressive posture may increase tension in the lower back and shoulder girdle during longer rides.
torso_low: Torso inclination ({measured:.1f}°) falls below the reference range ({ideal_min:.0f}°–{ideal_max:.0f}°), indicating an aerodynamic posture that demands solid spinal muscular tolerance.
torso_high: Torso posture is relatively upright ({measured:.1f}° compared to the {ideal_min:.0f}°–{ideal_max:.0f}° reference range). This configuration emphasizes lumbar relief and thoracic openness, though it presents increased aerodynamic drag.
torso_ok: Torso inclination ({measured:.1f}°) demonstrates balanced posture consistent with the discipline's geometry ({ideal_min:.0f}°–{ideal_max:.0f}°).
elbow_high: Elbows appear nearly locked ({measured:.1f}° compared to {ideal_min:.0f}°–{ideal_max:.0f}°). A slight bend is advisable to act as natural shock absorption against road surface vibrations.
elbow_low: Elbow flexion ({measured:.1f}°) is pronounced, which may suggest a short cockpit reach or excessive proximity to the handlebars.
elbow_ok: Upper limb flexion ({measured:.1f}°) provides a relaxed posture suited for road shock absorption.
kops_aligned: Knee-over-pedal-spindle (KOPS) alignment is well balanced relative to the pedal axle.
kops_forward: The knee is positioned {offset:.1f} mm ahead of the pedal spindle. Progressively sliding the saddle backward may encourage balanced load distribution to the posterior muscle chains.
kops_backward: The knee is positioned {offset:.1f} mm behind the pedal spindle. A slight forward saddle adjustment may assist pedaling cadence on steeper gradients.
kops_missing: KOPS alignment was not evaluated in this session.
cadence_power_format: Avg Cadence: {cadence} RPM | Avg Power: {power} W
plan_step_acclimation: Phase 1 (Week 1): Complete 2 to 3 light sessions of 45 to 60 minutes at a steady cadence (85–95 RPM) to encourage neuromuscular adaptation without acute overload.
plan_step_progression: Phase 2 (Week 2): Introduce steady endurance rides with moderate climbing, paying close attention to pelvic stability and hand pressure comfort.
plan_step_consolidation: Phase 3 (Week 3): Resume typical training intensity. If persistent discomfort or unusual strain occurs, an in-person professional bike fit is strongly recommended.
plan_step_maintenance: Maintain regular training routines and periodically monitor contact point wear (saddle, cleats, and cycling shoes).
